propositions.text: I grant this appeal and refer this matter back for re-determination by a different RPD member.
propositions.quote: I grant this appeal and refer this matter back for re-determination by a different RPD member for the reasons that follow.

paragraphs.summary: The court grants the appeal and refers the matter back for re-determination by a different RPD member.

propositions.text: The appellant is a Honduran citizen fearing harm from gunmen who killed his cousins.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Honduras. He fears that he would be killed or seriously harmed by gunmen who killed his cousins XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: The appellant witnessed the murder, fled Honduras to the US in 2014, was deported, re-entered US, then came to Canada in 2016 and claimed refugee status.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXXwitnessed the murder and ended up leaving Honduras for the United States in XXXX2014. He was then deported back to Honduras before entering the United States again in XXXX2014.... MrXXXX XXXX XXXXcrossed the border into Canada XXXX XXXX2016 and claimed refugee status a few months later.

propositions.text: The appellant's spouse received threatening calls in 2016, prompting suggestion to come to Canada.
propositions.quote: When Mr. XXXX XXXX told his spouse in 2016 that he intended to return to Honduras because he could not regularize his status in the United States, she told him that she had received two threatening calls in which the callers asked for him and said they would kill him. His spouse suggested that he come to Canada since her father lives here.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant is a Honduran fearing harm, witnessed murders, fled to US, was deported, re-entered US, then came to Canada after spouse received threats.

propositions.text: The RPD found credibility was determinative and found appellant not credible due to inconsistencies and omissions.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that credibility was a determinative issue in the case. The RPD found that Mr. XXXX XXXX was not credible due to the following: inconsistencies between his written narrative and the addresses and work information that he entered on one of his immigration forms; his omission to mention that the men who shot his cousins in 2012 ran after him and shot at him as he was running away; discrepancies between MrXXXX XXXX XXXX written narrative and a statement from his spouse about ongoing threats against him; and Mr. XXXX XXXX failure to obtain and disclose a copy of a report prepared by the police relating to his cousins' death.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found credibility determinative and found appellant not credible due to inconsistencies, omissions, discrepancies, and failure to disclose police report.

propositions.text: My role is to review all evidence and decide if RPD made correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

propositions.text: I agree there are reasons to question appellant's credibility but disagree with RPD's reasons for finding him not credible.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that there are reasons to question the credibility of the forward-looking risk that Mr. XXXX XXXX alleged in this case. However, I do not agree with the actual reasons provided by the RPD for finding Mr. XXXX XXXX not credible.

propositions.text: One credibility concern by RPD was correct but others were errors relying on peripheral matters and unexplained discrepancies.
propositions.quote: While one of the credibility concerns raised by the RPD was correct, I find that the RPD erred with respect to the other reasons it provided for finding Mr. XXXX XXXX not credible. In my view, the RPD erred in relying upon peripheral matters as well as a discrepancy that it did not provide Mr. XXXX XXXX an opportunity to explain.

propositions.text: This matter must be referred back to RPD for re-determination by a different member.
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out below, I find that this matter must be referred back to the RPD for re-determination by a different member.

propositions.text: The evidence presented by appellant is rejected.
propositions.quote: PROPOSED NEW EVIDENCE The evidence presented by Mr. XXXX XXXX is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court reviews evidence, agrees some credibility concerns exist but finds RPD erred on others, and refers matter back for re-determination, rejecting new evidence.

propositions.text: I can only accept evidence that arose after RPD decision, was not reasonably available then, or could not reasonably have been brought before RPD.
propositions.quote: According to the law,2 I can only accept evidence that: i. arose after the RPD decision; or ii. was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or iii. that the Appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal rule for accepting new evidence on appeal.

propositions.text: If evidence meets requirements, I must decide if it is new, credible and relevant before accepting it.
propositions.quote: If the evidence meets one or more of these requirements, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible and relevant before I can accept it.

propositions.text: RPD decision date is February 20, 2018, used to assess proposed new evidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD's decision in this case was February 20, 2018. This is the date to be used for the assessment of the proposed new evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains it must assess new evidence's novelty, credibility, and relevance using RPD decision date February 20, 2018.

propositions.text: Appellant's affidavit repeating his narrative is inadmissible as new evidence.
propositions.quote: When he filed his appeal record, Mr. XXXX XXXX representative submitted as proposed new evidence an affidavit in which he repeats the contents of his written narrative. This affidavit is not admissible as new evidence as it simply repeats the evidence in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's affidavit repeating his narrative inadmissible as new evidence.

propositions.text: Letter confirming appellant's employment in Honduras is inadmissible as new evidence due to no explanation for late submission.
propositions.quote: First, he sought to submit a letter confirming Mr. XXXX XXXX employment with a company in Honduras between January 2011 and August 2013. This letter is not admissible as new evidence as Mr. XXXX XXXX representative has provided no explanation as to why Mr. XXXX XXXX could not have obtained the letter sooner and file it with the RPD before it denied his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds employment letter inadmissible as new evidence due to no explanation for late submission.

propositions.text: Police complaint filed by spouse after 2012 incident is inadmissible as new evidence with no explanation for late submission and raises credibility concerns.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX also filed a police complaint apparently made by his spouse after the incident in XXXX2012 when his cousins were shot. This document is also inadmissible. Mr. XXXX XXXX has provided no explanation as to why he could not have obtained this document earlier and file it with the RPD. I also note that the document raises credibility concerns as Mr. XXXX XXXX made no mention of his spouse having complained to the police when the RPD asked whether the killings had been reported to the police.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police complaint inadmissible as new evidence with no explanation for late submission and notes credibility concerns.

propositions.text: Affidavit by friend dated April 2018 is inadmissible as new evidence because information predates RPD decision and no explanation for late submission.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX also filed an affidavit sworn by a friend in April 2018 in which a friend relates his understanding that Mr. XXXX XXXX life is at risk due to his having witnessed the killing of his cousins in 2012. This document is also inadmissible. Although the affidavit postdates the RPD decision in this case, the information in the affidavit predates the decision. Mr. XXXX XXXX has provided no explanation as to why he did not obtain this document earlier and file it with the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds friend's affidavit inadmissible as new evidence because information predates RPD decision and no explanation for late submission.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in finding credibility undermined by inconsistency between narrative and immigration forms.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX argues that the RPD erred in finding that his credibility was undermined by an inconsistency between his written narrative and the addresses and employment information he provided on one of his immigration forms.

propositions.text: I do not agree with appellant's argument on this point.
propositions.quote: I do not agree.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred on credibility due to inconsistency; the court disagrees.

propositions.text: Appellant indicated residence and spouse's residence on immigration forms and narrative with some differences in locations and dates.
propositions.quote: MrXXXX XXXX XXXX indicated on one of his immigration forms that he lived in the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX until he left Honduras in XXXX XXXX. In addition, on his Basis of Claim form, he stated that his spouse and children were living in XXXX XXXX. In his narrative, he stated that he was born in the department XXXX XXXX XXXX but, after the killing of his cousins, he moved his spouse and children to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX2013 and began to work in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX2013.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes appellant's stated residences and dates on forms and narrative with some differences.

propositions.text: Appellant filed amendment to narrative and Basis of Claim form to correct omissions about residence.
propositions.quote: Prior to the hearing, he filed an amendment to his narrative in which he indicated that he had failed to note on his immigration form that he had XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. He indicated that he did not realize the importance of noting that information in his immigration form. In addition, he sought to amend his Basis of Claim form to indicate that his spouse XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant amended narrative and Basis of Claim form to correct omissions about residence.

propositions.text: Appellant failed to satisfactorily explain inconsistencies between narrative and immigration forms about residence.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that MrXXXX XXXX XXXX failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the inconsistencies between his narrative, on the one hand, and the information he provided on his immigration form and Basis of Claim form about his residence as well as the residence of his spouse and children.

propositions.text: This inconsistency alone is insufficient to find general lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: However, I do not find that this inconsistency is of sufficient importance, on its own, to make a general finding of lack of credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees appellant failed to explain inconsistencies but finds this alone insufficient to find lack of credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant's narrative and testimony state gunmen shot cousins, saw him, and he ran to hide; he testified gunmen ran after him but did not reach him.
propositions.quote: In his written narrative, Mr. XXXX XXXX states that he was face to face with the gun men when they shot his cousins and that he ran from the place in order to hide. Likewise, at the hearing, MrXXXX XXXX XXXX testified that the gunmen saw him and that he ran to escape after he saw his cousins killed. When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX XXXX whether the gunmen also tried to shoot at him, he said yes, that they ran after him but were not able to reach him.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts appellant's narrative and testimony about gunmen shooting cousins and chasing him but not reaching him.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's omission of mention that gunmen ran after him and shot at him in narrative undermined credibility or that testimony was embellishment.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that Mr. XXXX XXXX omission of any mention that the gunmen ran after him and shot at him in his written narrative negatively affected his credibility, or conversely, his embellishment of his claim in his testimony undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: RPD stated appellant explained omission by saying he was forgetful.
propositions.quote: The RPD stated that, when asked to explain the omission, Mr. XXXX XXXX stated that it was because he was forgetful.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found omission or embellishment undermined credibility and that appellant said omission was due to forgetfulness.

propositions.text: RPD misrepresented appellant's evidence about gunmen shooting at him and his explanation for omission.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD misrepresented Mr. XXXX XXXX evidence.

propositions.text: Appellant said gunmen ran after him and RPD did not clarify if they also shot at him.
propositions.quote: although he responded "yes" to the RPD's question as to whether the gunmen shot at him, he went on to say that they ran after him. The RPD did not follow up to clarify whether he was alleging that the gunmen also shot at him or simply ran after him.

propositions.text: Appellant explained omission as due to many things on his mind and trauma, not simply forgetfulness.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX did not simply state that he was forgetful when asked for an explanation for the omission. Mr. XXXX XXXX stated that there were too many things on his mind, that he has forgotten a lot of things, and that he is not the same person since seeing what he saw that day.

propositions.text: This explanation is not the same as simply saying he was forgetful.
propositions.quote: This is not the same thing as simply saying that he was forgetful.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD misrepresented appellant's evidence and explanation for omission, which involved trauma, not mere forgetfulness.

propositions.text: Omitted information is additional detail; core claim is gunmen saw him and want to kill him for witnessing murders.
propositions.quote: I find that the information omitted from Mr. XXXX XXXX written narrative is in the nature of additional details. While being chased and shot at are important details, the core of MrXXXX XXXX XXXX claim is that the gunmen saw him on the day that they shot his cousins and that they would still wish to kill him because he witnessed the murders.

propositions.text: RPD erred in finding omission of peripheral details undermined credibility.
propositions.quote: In my view, the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX XXXX omission of additional peripheral details in his narrative undermined his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds omitted details are peripheral and RPD erred in finding omission undermined credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in finding credibility negatively affected by discrepancy between his narrative and spouse's statement about death threats.
propositions.quote: I agree with Mr. XXXX XXXX representative that the RPD erred in finding that his credibility was negatively affected by a discrepancy between his written narrative and the statement he submitted from his spouse on the issue of whether he continued to receive death threats.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred in finding credibility affected by discrepancy between his narrative and spouse's statement about death threats.

propositions.text: Appellant's narrative says spouse received two threats and suggested he come to Canada; spouse's statement says appellant received calls in US and she also received calls, prompting contact with her father in Canada.
propositions.quote: In his written narrative, Mr. XXXX XXXX does not mention receiving any death threats when he was in the United States and he states that his spouse suggested he come to Canada because she had received two threats. In her statement, his spouse states that Mr. XXXX XXXX received a call when he first arrived in the United States and that she was also receiving calls. She then states, "[s]ince my husband was also receiving calls in the United States, I decided to contact my father [...] in Canada."

paragraphs.summary: The court describes discrepancy: appellant's narrative omits his threats in US; spouse's statement says he received calls in US, prompting contact with her father in Canada.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by relying on an apparent discrepancy without giving Mr. XXXX XXXX a chance to explain it.
propositions.quote: I agree with Mr. XXXX XXXX that the RPD erred in relying on this apparent discrepancy without providing him with a chance to explain it.

propositions.text: The spouse's statement was unclear about the number of calls when first arriving in the US.
propositions.quote: the statement from Mr. XXXX XXXX spouse is not clear as to whether there was just one call when he first arrived in the United States or more calls.

propositions.text: The RPD should have allowed Mr. XXXX XXXX to explain before relying on the discrepancy for credibility findings.
propositions.quote: all of this should have been put to Mr. XXXX XXXX to provide him with the opportunity to provide an explanation before the RPD relied upon this apparent discrepancy as one of just a few reasons why it found Mr. XXXX XXXX not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred by relying on an unexplained discrepancy and should have allowed Mr. XXXX XXXX to explain it, noting the spouse's statement was unclear.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in drawing a negative credibility inference from failure to file a police report confirming cousins' deaths.
propositions.quote: I agree with Mr. XXXX XXXX representative that the RPD erred in drawing a negative inference as to credibility due to Mr. XXXX XXXX failure to obtain and file a copy of a report in which the police confirmed his cousins' deaths in 2012.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX XXXX filed death certificates and a burial document for his two cousins.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX had in fact filed death certificates for his two cousins as well as a document attesting to the burial of one of the two cousins.

propositions.text: The RPD did not mention these documents and its negative finding cannot stand given the other documents filed.
propositions.quote: The RPD makes no mention of the death certificates or the burial document in its decision. In my view, its finding in relation to his failure to file a copy of the report in which the police confirmed the deaths cannot stand given his filing of the other documents with which the RPD took no issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred by negatively inferring credibility from failure to file a police report, ignoring death certificates and burial documents filed.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to address the main issue of forward-looking risk from the gunmen if Mr. XXXX XXXX returns to Honduras.
propositions.quote: Due to its reliance upon peripheral matters, the RPD failed to adequately address the main issue in this case which is whether there is sufficient credible evidence to establish that Mr. XXXX XXXX would likely face a forward-looking risk at the hands of these gunmen if he were to return to Honduras today.

propositions.text: The killing of Mr. XXXX XXXX cousins occurred eight years ago by three unknown men.
propositions.quote: The alleged killing of Mr. XXXX XXXXcousins occurred eight years ago and it was carried out by three unknown men.

propositions.text: No evidence beyond Mr. XXXX XXXX's belief established the gunmen's connection to organized crime.
propositions.quote: Although Mr. XXXX XXXX alleged that the three men were connected to organized crime, there was no evidence beyond his own belief to establish this connection.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD failed to address forward-looking risk adequately and notes the killing was eight years ago by unknown men with no evidence of organized crime links.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by not allowing Mr. XXXX XXXX to testify about general country conditions in Honduras.
propositions.quote: While the RPD may legitimately discount MrXXXX XXXX XXXX evidence if it finds it speculative or outside the scope of his own personal knowledge, it cannot simply forbid him from testifying as to the conditions in his country.

propositions.text: The RPD cannot know the relevance or probative value of country condition evidence before hearing it.
propositions.quote: The RPD cannot know whether his evidence lacked relevance or probative value before hearing it.

propositions.text: The RPD might grant little weight to such evidence but cannot forbid any testimony about country conditions.
propositions.quote: In sum, the RPD might legitimately grant little weight to Mr. XXXX XXXX evidence regarding the conditions in his country but it cannot legitimately forbid him from providing any testimony as to these conditions.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred by forbidding testimony on country conditions, which it must hear before assessing relevance or weight.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony is presumed true unless valid reasons exist to doubt it.
propositions.quote: A claimant's testimony is presumed to be true unless there are valid reasons to doubt its truthfulness.

propositions.text: The RPD was correct to draw a negative inference from inconsistencies about relocation after the cousins' shooting.
propositions.quote: the RPD was correct to draw a negative inference as to credibility due to the inconsistencies in Mr. XXXX XXXX evidence regarding whether he and his spouse and children had relocated to a different department after the shooting of his cousins.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by relying on peripheral matters and an unexplained discrepancy without allowing explanation.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in relying on peripheral matters as well as an apparent discrepancy which it did not provide him with a chance to explain.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to address forward-looking risk adequately due to focus on peripheral matters and disallowing testimony on Honduras conditions.
propositions.quote: It also failed to adequately address the issue of forward-looking risk due to its focus on peripheral matters and its disallowance of any testimony regarding conditions in Honduras.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD rightly doubted relocation inconsistencies but erred relying on peripheral matters and disallowing testimony on country conditions.

propositions.text: The RAD cannot make a final determination on this claim within its jurisdictional limits.
propositions.quote: In my view, it is not possible within the jurisdictional confines of the RAD, to make a final determination on this claim.

propositions.text: The inconsistency about place of residence alone is insufficient to find general lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the inconsistency relating to Mr. XXXX XXXX place of residence is insufficient, on its own, to give rise to a general finding of lack of credibility.

propositions.text: Even if the account of witnessing cousins' death is credible, forward-looking risk remains inadequately explored.
propositions.quote: However, even if I were to find that Mr. XXXX XXXX account of his witnessing of his cousins' death was credible, the issue of whether he would face a forward-looking risk in Honduras remains to be adequately explored in this case.

propositions.text: The RAD may remit cases to the RPD for re-determination when it cannot confirm or substitute decisions without hearing evidence.
propositions.quote: When the RAD is unable to confirm, or set aside and substitute its own decision without hearing evidence that was presented to the RPD, the RAD may return the case to the RPD for re-determination.

propositions.text: The RAD must remit this matter to the RPD for re-determination in these circumstances.
propositions.quote: In the circumstances of this case, the RAD is left with no option but to remit this matter to the RPD for re-determination.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RAD cannot decide finally and must remit the matter to the RPD for re-determination due to unresolved credibility and risk issues.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed and the matter is referred back to the RPD for re-determination by a different member.
propositions.quote: I allow the appeal and refer this matter back to the RPD re-determination by a different member taking into account the findings set out above.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal and refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a different member.
